ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Tips for Making a Habit Stick

fullPassage:
Tips for Making a Habit Stick

Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start small. Don't try to do too much, too quickly. A habit is formed through repetition, so make the change easier to repeat. Second, make your goal specific. Don't say, "I'll meditate regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." This works even better if you combine your new habit with an existing one, for example, "After brushing my teeth in the morning, I'll meditate for five minutes." When your fixed habit becomes a cue for action, your new habit is more likely to stick. Third, make it attractive. Pair your new change with what you love. You could listen to your favorite piece of calming music while meditating. Fourth, track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of achievement and helps you keep going. Fifth, be flexible. Forming a new habit takes time. If you find that your progress has stopped for any reason, just pick up where you left off.

questions.passage: Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start small. Don't try to do too much, too quickly. A habit is formed through (A)[repetition / innovation], so make the change easier to (B)[repeat / avoid]. Second, make your goal (C)[specific / vague].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 습관은 반복을 통해 형성되므로, 변화를 반복하기 쉽게 만들어라. 목표를 구체적으로 만들어라.
det.analysis:
✅ ① repetition — repeat — specific
❌ ② innovation — repeat — vague
❌ ③ repetition — avoid — vague
❌ ④ innovation — avoid — specific
✅ (A) repetition: 습관은 반복을 통해 형성. (B) repeat: 반복하기 쉽게. (C) specific: 목표를 구체적으로.
det.tip: repetition(반복) ↔ innovation(혁신). repeat(반복하다) ↔ avoid(피하다). specific(구체적) ↔ vague(모호한).

questions.passage: This works even better if you (A)[combine / separate] your new habit with an existing one. When your fixed habit becomes a cue for action, your new habit is more likely to stick. Third, make it (B)[attractive / repulsive]. Pair your new change with what you love. You could listen to your favorite piece of (C)[calming / disturbing] music while meditating.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 새 습관을 기존 습관과 결합하라. 습관을 매력적으로 만들어라. 차분한 음악을 들어라.
det.analysis:
✅ ① combine — attractive — calming
❌ ② separate — attractive — disturbing
❌ ③ combine — repulsive — disturbing
❌ ④ separate — repulsive — calming
✅ (A) combine: 기존 습관과 결합. (B) attractive: 매력적으로 만들기. (C) calming: 차분한 음악.
det.tip: combine(결합) ↔ separate(분리). attractive(매력적) ↔ repulsive(역겨운). calming(차분한) ↔ disturbing(불안한).

questions.passage: Fourth, track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of (A)[achievement / failure] and helps you keep going. Fifth, be (B)[flexible / rigid]. Forming a new habit takes time. If you find that your progress has stopped for any reason, just pick up where you (C)[left off / gave up].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 진행 상황을 보면 성취감을 느끼게 된다. 유연해져라. 멈춘 곳에서 다시 시작하라.
det.analysis:
✅ ① achievement — flexible — left off
❌ ② failure — flexible — gave up
❌ ③ achievement — rigid — gave up
❌ ④ failure — rigid — left off
✅ (A) achievement: 성취감. (B) flexible: 유연. (C) left off: 멈춘 곳에서 다시.
det.tip: achievement(성취) ↔ failure(실패). flexible(유연한) ↔ rigid(경직된). left off(중단한) ↔ gave up(포기한).

questions.passage: Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start small. Don't try to do too much, too quickly. A habit is formed through ①<u>repetition</u>, so make the change easier to ②<u>repeat</u>. Second, make your goal ③<u>specific</u>. Don't say, "I'll meditate regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." This works even better if you ④<u>separate</u> your new habit with an existing one.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 새 습관을 기존 습관과 결합(combine)하면 더 효과적이다. separate(분리하다)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①repetition: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②repeat: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③specific: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④separate: 원문은 combine. 습관을 결합하는 것이 핵심.
det.tip: combine(결합하다) ↔ separate(분리하다). 새 습관+기존 습관 결합이 포인트.

questions.passage: When your fixed habit becomes a cue for action, your new habit is more likely to stick. Third, make it attractive. Pair your new change with what you love. You could listen to your favorite piece of ①<u>calming</u> music while meditating. Fourth, ②<u>track</u> your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of ③<u>achievement</u> and helps you ④<u>stop</u> going.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 진행 상황을 보면 성취감을 느끼고 계속(keep) 할 수 있다. stop(멈추다)은 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①calming: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②track: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③achievement: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④stop: 원문은 keep. 계속 나아가게 도와준다는 맥락.
det.tip: keep going(계속 나아가다) ↔ stop going(멈추다). 긍정적 맥락에서 stop은 부적절.

questions.passage: Second, make your goal specific. Don't say, "I'll meditate regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." This works even better if you combine your new habit with an ①<u>existing</u> one, for example, "After brushing my teeth in the morning, I'll meditate for five minutes." When your ②<u>fixed</u> habit becomes a ③<u>cue</u> for action, your new habit is more ④<u>unlikely</u> to stick.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 새 습관이 자리 잡을 가능성이 더 높다(likely). unlikely(~할 것 같지 않은)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①existing: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②fixed: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③cue: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④unlikely: 원문은 likely. 결합하면 습관이 잘 자리 잡는다는 긍정적 맥락.
det.tip: likely(~할 것 같은) ↔ unlikely(~할 것 같지 않은). more likely to stick = 자리 잡을 가능성이 높다.

questions.stem: (A)의 'sticks'와 (B)의 'going'의 의미를 가장 잘 나타낸 것은?

det.korean: (A) 정말 자리 잡는 습관. (B) 계속 나아가게 도와준다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 붙이다 — (B) 출발하다
✅ ② (A) 자리 잡다 — (B) 계속하다
❌ ③ (A) 찌르다 — (B) 이동하다
❌ ④ (A) 자리 잡다 — (B) 출발하다
✅ ② (A) 자리 잡다: stick = 습관이 자리 잡다. (B) 계속하다: keep going = 계속 나아가다.
det.tip: stick: ①붙이다 ②자리 잡다/지속되다. going: ①가다 ②계속하다.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the act of doing something again and again in order to learn or improve"

det.korean: "배우거나 향상하기 위해 무언가를 반복하는 행위" = 반복.
det.analysis: ✅ ④repetition: 반복. 정의와 일치. ❌ ①achievement(성취): 무관. ❌ ②meditation(명상): 무관. ❌ ③flexibility(유연성): 무관.
det.tip: repetition: 반복. 본문 'A habit is formed through repetition'에서 등장.

questions.passage: Fourth, track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of __________.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

Her greatest __________ (achieve) was winning the national spelling bee.

det.korean: 그녀의 가장 큰 성취는 전국 스펠링 비 우승이었다.
det.analysis: ✅ achievement: 소유격 Her + greatest + __________ → 명사 필요. achieve(동사) → achievement(명사).
det.tip: achieve(동사: 성취하다) → achievement(명사: 성취, 업적).

다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

The yoga class improved her __________ (flexible) and balance significantly.

det.korean: 요가 수업이 그녀의 유연성과 균형감을 크게 향상시켰다.
det.analysis: ✅ flexibility: 소유격 her + __________ + and balance → 명사 필요. flexible(형용사) → flexibility(명사).
det.tip: flexible(형용사: 유연한) → flexibility(명사: 유연성).

questions.passage:
Tips for Making a Habit Stick

Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start small. Don't try to do too much, too quickly. A habit is formed through repetition, so make ____. Second, make your goal specific. Don't say, "I'll meditate regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." This works even better if you combine your new habit with an existing one, for example, "After brushing my teeth in the morning, I'll meditate for five minutes." When your fixed habit becomes a cue for action, your new habit is more likely to stick. Third, make it attractive. Pair your new change with what you love. You could listen to your favorite piece of calming music while meditating. Fourth, track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of achievement and helps you keep going. Fifth, be flexible. Forming a new habit takes time. If you find that your progress has stopped for any reason, just pick up where you left off.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 변화를 반복하기 쉽게 만들어라.
det.analysis: ✅ ③the change easier to repeat: 원문 그대로. 반복이 핵심. ❌ ①ambitious: 작게 시작하라는 맥락과 반대. ❌ ②complex: 반대. ❌ ④strict: 유연성과 반대.
det.tip: start small → make the change easier to repeat. 작게 시작 = 반복 용이.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 새 습관이 자리 잡을 가능성이 더 높다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① more likely to stick: 기존 습관이 신호(cue)가 되면 새 습관이 자리 잡을 가능성이 높아진다는 의미로 문맥에 적합
❌ ② impossible to maintain: "유지하기 불가능하다"는 의미로 반대
❌ ③ harder to remember: "기억하기 더 어렵다"는 의미로 무관
❌ ④ less important than before: "예전보다 덜 중요하다"는 의미로 무관
det.tip: cue for action → more likely to stick. 신호 → 습관 정착.
